next_step: Deliver dedicated capacity sizing + 6-week POC plan; schedule perf baseline (p95/p99) test window
notes:
Account intro: SlateForge builds an IDE-centric copilot for enterprise engineering teams (JetBrains + VS Code plugins). Primary ask: Dedicated capacity to guarantee low-latency streaming completions during peak developer hours and predictable token economics.

Summary of requirements (customer language / paraphrase):
- "Ideal: <80ms per-token tail latency for streaming completions within IDE while preserving high-quality completions."
- "Need deterministic latency during 10:00-12:30 and 15:00-18:00 PT — we have developer spikes at commit/review windows."
- Model/version pinning is critical: must be able to pin to particular model hash for reproducible assistant behavior (and roll back to previous pinned model).
- Fallbacks: when dedicated pool hits capacity, fall back to a quantized smaller variant rather than blocking completions.
- Cost sensitivity: want predictable monthly cost for committed capacity + clear burst billing model.
- Security: SSO/SAML + SCIM, audit logs for each API call, KMS integration, 90-day retention for telemetry.

POC ask: 6-week pilot with ~50 internal devs (can expand to 200 in week 5). Scope: integration test (VS Code & IntelliJ), streaming SDK evaluation (SSE + gRPC), perf baseline (p50/p95/p99 token latencies), and quality spot-checks on completion accuracy.

Recent timeline / interactions (bulleted):
- 2024-12-01: Intro call (AE Maya + SE Daniel) — product fit looks strong; customer delivered initial architecture diagram.
- 2024-12-08: Security kickoff — customer sent SSO/SAML metadata and CC'd security@slateforge.
- 2025-01-10: Technical deep-dive with infra team — discussed Dedicated pool sizing, autoscale windows, and burst policies; agreed to baseline token rates.
- 2025-01-29: Meeting w/ Eng Director (Fireflies ff-2025-01-29-8841) — asked for production-like jitter tests and 99th percentile latency guarantees during bursts.
- 2025-02-03: Shared draft pricing + sizing (drive/slateforge/Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_v2.pdf).
- 2025-02-10: Customer ran internal smoke test against hosted API; reported increased jitter during simulated peak. Logged Jira INF-4821.

Technical targets & constraints (explicit):
- Throughput: initial commit for POC = 50 concurrent devs, average 8 tokens/sec per session; peak design target = 600 concurrent sessions (month 3).
- p95 token latency target: <80ms; p99 goal: <150ms for streaming token delivery.
- Max sustained token throughput for dedicated pool requested during POC: ~12M tokens/day with burst headroom to 18M/day.
- Model: prefer Redwood-verified 7B/13B open models; must support 4-bit quantized fallback for cost/burst.
- Session stickiness: want KV-cache affinity to reduce repeated prefix cost for long-lived IDE sessions.

Operational & rollout notes:
- Prefer dedicated GPU pool in us-west + eu-west for latency-sensitive routing.
- Need canary rollout for model updates (pin current model -> deploy new -> A/B small % -> auto-fallback on quality regression).
- Observability: require token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards.

Negotiation points / price sensitivity:
- Customer expects committed capacity discount for 12-month term; flexible on upfront vs monthly billing.
- Wants explicit burst policy: e.g., baseline capacity handles X concurrent devs; burst to Y for short windows (minute-level) without degrading SLA.

Next steps (short):
- [Action] Redwood SE (Daniel) to deliver dedicated sizing config + latency simulation script by 2025-02-18.
- [Action] Product to confirm model pin & rollback API details (including manifest/hash semantics) and share docs.
- [Action] Security to provide SOC2 + KMS integration checklist; SlateForge to return signatures by 2025-02-28.
- Schedule 2-hour perf run (canary) for week of 2025-02-24; customer will provide test tokens and request simulator.

Notes flavor: shorthand, inline quotes captured from Eng Director: "We'd rather have predictable latency than occasional cheaper tokens — dev experience matters more." Also: "If you can prove stable p99 under burst, procurement is straightforward."

POC success criteria (customer):
- Sustained p95 < 80ms over 2-hour simulated peak with 200 concurrent sessions.
- No authorization/SSO failures in integration tests.
- Cost per active dev within quoted ARR band (<= $X per seat/month as proposed).

Open questions for Redwood:
- Exact format of burst billing and soft vs hard limits?
- How long are pinned model artifacts stored / how do we snapshot KV caches for rollback?
- EU data residency: can we isolate telemetry + logs to eu-west for EU users?

CRM style summary: good fit for Dedicated. Security is the gating item. Procurement timeline optimistic: POC Feb->Mar, procurement decision Q2.
